The 18th-century French engineer Augustin Fresnel designed a lens that could gather more light and send it out as a narrow, powerful beam, and it was the first to use a prism to bend the light. The 19th-century Swiss engineer Aime Argand used a lens with a hollow circular wick to keep the flame from spreading, and it was the first to use a lens with prisms to focus the light. Lighthouse history is a long and complex one. The first lighthouse was built in the third century BC on the island of Pharos in Egypt. Over time, lighthouses were built on land and sea, with different designs and technologies emerging. The first Fresnel lens was invented in the 1820s, and it revolutionized the design of lighthouses.

The history of lighthouses dates back to ancient times when sailors used fires on hills to guide ships. The Pharos of Alexandria, built in the 3rd century BC, was the most famous early lighthouse and stood for over a thousand years.
